title: Hull Speed Calculator
description: Estimate theoretical hull speed from waterline length using the classic 1.34 × √LWL rule for displacement hulls.
formula: Classical displacement estimate: V ≈ 1.34√LWL (knots, LWL in feet). Planing hulls and multihulls often exceed this.
formulaDetail: Based on Froude number ~0.4 for typical monohull wave-making resistance.

faq.question: Is hull speed a hard limit?
faq.answer: No. It is a useful rule of thumb for displacement monohulls. Light air, surfing, or planing can yield higher speeds.

title: Initial Bearing Calculator
description: Compute the initial true bearing from one lat/lon waypoint to another (the great-circle route's starting bearing).

engine.formulaDisplay: Forward azimuth via spherical trigonometry (atan2 of sin/cos terms)

formula: Initial bearing uses the standard forward azimuth formula between two geographic points on a sphere.
formulaDetail: Does not apply variation/deviation; output is true bearing. This calculation uses spherical-Earth geometry and is an approximation of the corresponding ellipsoidal geodesic bearing.
examples: Use with great-circle distance for route sketching

faq.question: Does bearing stay constant along the route?
faq.answer: No. Great-circle routes change bearing along the arc; this value is only the starting heading.

title: Rhumb Line Distance Calculator
description: Approximate rhumb-line distance in nautical miles between two positions (plane sailing at mean latitude).
formula: Rhumb line maintains constant bearing; this is a mid-latitude plane approximation, not exact Mercator sailing.
formulaDetail: For short legs it is close to GPS track distance; for ocean legs prefer great-circle tools.
examples: Small coastal hops: compare to chart divider distance

faq.question: When is rhumb line used?
faq.answer: Mercator charts plot rhumb lines as straight segments; many short legs are steered nearly rhumb.

title: Statute Miles to Nautical Miles Converter
description: Convert statute (land) miles to nautical miles using 1 nm = 1.15078 statute miles.
formula: 1 nautical mile ≈ 1.15078 statute miles, so nm = sm × 0.868976.
formulaDetail: Nautical miles align with latitude minutes; statute miles are the common US/UK land mile.

faq.question: Why two mile types?
faq.answer: Marine navigation uses nautical miles tied to latitude; road and many maps use statute miles.

title: Celsius to Fahrenheit Converter
description: Convert air or water temperature between °C and °F for forecasts, logs, and crew briefings.
formula: Linear conversion between Celsius and Fahrenheit scales.

faq.question: Is this exact?
faq.answer: Yes for everyday temperatures; it is the definition of the Fahrenheit scale relative to Celsius.

title: Feet to Meters Converter
description: Convert feet to meters (and vice versa) for dock lines, mast heights, and bridge clearances.
formula: International foot definition: 0.3048 meters per foot.

title: Latitude Degrees to Nautical Miles
description: Convert degrees of latitude (or longitude at the equator) to nautical miles along a meridian.
formula: One degree of latitude is approximately 60 nautical miles (one minute ≈ one nm); the exact length varies slightly with latitude on the reference ellipsoid.
formulaDetail: Longitude distance varies with cos(latitude); this tool is for latitude or equator longitude.

faq.question: Does this work for longitude everywhere?
faq.answer: Only at the equator. Elsewhere use cos(latitude) scaling or a rhumb/great-circle tool.

title: VMG Calculator
description: Velocity made good toward a mark: boat speed × cos(angle off bow to the mark).

engine.formulaDisplay: VMG = BSP × cos(θ), θ from bow toward mark

formula: VMG is the component of velocity toward a waypoint along your heading-to-mark geometry.
formulaDetail: 0° = dead ahead; 90° = VMG 0 toward mark along heading (pure beam reach to mark geometry).

title: Fuel Range Calculator (Nautical Miles)
description: Estimate range in nautical miles from cruising speed, fuel aboard, and consumption rate.
formula: Time available = fuel ÷ burn rate; range = speed × time when speed is steady in knots.

faq.question: Should I add reserve?
faq.answer: Yes—plan 10–30% fuel reserve depending on passage and weather.

title: Anchor Shackle to Feet Calculator
description: Convert anchor chain shackles (15 fathoms each) to total feet of rode.
formula: US Navy / common shipping: 1 shackle of chain = 15 fathoms = 90 feet.
formulaDetail: Shackle length varies by maritime convention; verify the convention used for the vessel, chart, or reference material.

title: Bar to PSI Converter
description: Convert pressure in bar to pounds per square inch for gauges and systems.

title: Liters to US Gallons Converter
description: Convert liters to US gallons for fuel tanks and water tanks.
formula: US liquid gallon conversion for tank planning.

faq.question: Imperial gallons?
faq.answer: This uses US gallons. Imperial (UK) gallons are larger; use a dedicated converter if needed.

title: Cables to Nautical Miles Converter
description: Convert cables (1/10 nm) to nautical miles for chart and pilotage notation.
formula: The cable (tenth of a nautical mile) is still seen in some charting and naval usage.
formulaDetail: A cable is commonly treated as 0.1 nautical mile (185.2 m) in modern maritime usage, but historical and national conventions can differ.

title: Geographic Range of a Light Calculator
description: Estimate combined geographic visible range (nm) from height of eye and light elevation.
formula: Optical geographic range sums horizon distances from observer and light. Atmospheric conditions and light power alter actual sighting.
examples: 9 ft eye, 80 ft light → ~14.0 nm combined geometric range

faq.question: Is this luminous range?
faq.answer: No—this is geometric horizon range. Nominal range depends on light intensity and visibility.

title: Radar Horizon Calculator
description: Approximate radar line-of-sight horizon in nautical miles from antenna height.

engine.formulaDisplay: Approximate radar horizon: d (nm) ≈ 1.23 × √(h / 0.3048), where h is antenna height in meters.

formula: Empirical radar horizon approximation; target detectability also depends on power, sea clutter, and target height.
formulaDetail: This is an approximate radar-horizon calculation using a standard 4/3-Earth-radius atmospheric-refraction model; actual radar range can vary with atmospheric conditions, antenna height, and target characteristics.
examples: 12 m scanner → ~7.7 nm to the sea surface.

title: Current Drift Distance Calculator
description: Distance run by set in nautical miles: current speed × time in hours.
formula: If set is steady and perpendicular to intended track, this estimates offset magnitude over time.
formulaDetail: Real vectors need angle to course for cross-track error.

title: Sail Area to Displacement Ratio
description: Classic ratio SA ÷ DISPL^(2/3) with displacement in pounds (not long tons).
formula: Higher SA/D generally indicates a more powerful rig relative to hull displacement (light-air performance vs stiffness tradeoffs).
examples: Typical cruisers often fall in teens–low twenties depending on design

title: Capsize Screening Factor
description: Simple beam / (DISPL/64)^(1/3) style screening number (displacement in pounds).

engine.formulaDisplay: Beam ÷ cube root of (displacement in cubic feet from lb/64)

formula: Historical rule-of-thumb screening; not a substitute for stability letters, STIX, or naval architecture review.
examples: Lower values often correlate with offshore-oriented designs in popular literature—verify with official data

faq.question: Is this certification?
faq.answer: No. It is an approximate comparative index only.

title: Pounds to Kilograms Converter
description: Convert weight in pounds to kilograms for provisions, ground tackle, and cargo.
formula: International avoirdupois pound to kilogram conversion.

title: Kilowatts to Horsepower Converter
description: Convert engine power kW to mechanical horsepower for marine diesels and electric drives.
formula: Mechanical horsepower conversion commonly used for propulsion comparisons.

title: Meters per Second to Knots Converter
description: Convert m/s to knots for scientific wind data or current models.
formula: Exact knot definition via nautical mile per hour vs SI meters per second.

title: Inches of Mercury to Millibar Converter
description: Convert inHg to hPa/mbar for barometers and weather maps.
formula: Standard conversion between US mercury barometer units and millibars.

title: Bilge Pump Time Calculator
description: Minutes to move a volume at a given pump rate (US gal, GPM).
formula: Idealized steady pump rate; hose lift and strainer clogging reduce real flow.

title: Wavelength from Wave Period
description: Deep-water wavelength from period using L = gT²/(2π).
formula: Dispersion relation for deep-water gravity waves; shallow water shortens wavelength at fixed period.

title: Longitude Minutes to Nautical Miles
description: Nautical miles per minute of longitude at a given latitude (cosine scaling).
formula: At the equator, 1' longitude = 1 nm; at latitude φ, east-west distance per minute shrinks by cos(φ).

title: True from Magnetic Heading
description: True heading = magnetic heading + easterly variation (subtract westerly).
formula: Variation (declination) converts between magnetic and true directions. Deviation is additional ship-specific error.
examples: 270° mag, 10°W variation → enter −10 for var → 260° true

faq.question: What about deviation?
faq.answer: Apply deviation from the compass card after magnetic correction, or combine into a single correction per your procedure.

title: Cross Track Error Calculator
description: Approximate XTE in nm from distance run along track and bearing error.
formula: Small-angle linearized cross-track estimate for quick mental checks.

title: Speed Over Ground Calculator
description: Vector sum of speed through water and current using law of cosines.
formula: θ is the angle between velocity vectors of boat through water and water movement (set).
examples: 6 kn STW + 1.5 kn current at 45° → ~7.1 kn SOG (illustrative)

title: Mercator Scale Factor Calculator
description: Chart scale exaggeration k = sec(φ) at a given latitude.
formula: On a Mercator chart, scale expands away from the equator; k is the linear exaggeration at latitude φ.
formulaDetail: This calculation uses the spherical Mercator model and does not account for ellipsoidal geodesic corrections.

title: Feet of Rode to Shackles
description: Convert deployed rode length in feet to standard anchor shackles (90 ft each).
formula: Common anchor chain marking: 1 shackle = 15 fathoms = 90 feet.
formulaDetail: Shackle length varies by maritime convention; verify the convention used for the vessel, chart, or reference material.

title: Square Feet to Square Meters Converter
description: Convert sail area or deck area between ft² and m².
formula: Area conversion using international foot definition.

title: Cubic Feet to Liters Converter
description: Tank volume conversion for bilge, water, or fuel compartments.
formula: Cubic foot to liter conversion for capacity planning.
